title: Matching Rules for a Three-Dimensional Strongly Aperiodic Monotile
abstract: A recent pre-print [arXiv:2609.19214] proposed a three-dimensional (3D) strongly aperiodic monotile: a shape that tiles Euclidean space only aperiodically and which admits no symmetry of infinite order. The proof takes the 3D Chair tile identified previously by Lee and Moody, and adds geometric decorations to the faces so as to force aperiodicity (without these decorations The Chair also admits periodic tilings). Here we establish general requirements on face decorations to achieve the same end, in order to facilitate the search for physical realisations. We find that the requirements are minimal. We provide matching rules using three colours of arrow. They are not equivalent to the original rules, but force the same tiling by forcing Chairs to compose into `Superchairs' with doubled linear dimensions. In this process the matching rules themselves compose uniquely, which is the core of the earlier proof. Relaxing this constraint further we find that the same structure can be forced using only a matching rule based on the colours of squares, regardless of orientation. Any physical system encoding these rules (geometrically or otherwise) will force the strongly aperiodic monotiling. We provide simple examples.
summary: This paper develops and simplifies the matching rules required to force a strongly aperiodic tiling using a 3D monotile called the Decorated Chair. By moving from complex geometric rules to simple face-coloring constraints, the authors prove that the tiling's aperiodicity is robustly encoded in these minimal local rules. This work provides a theoretical framework for designing physical systems that exhibit complex, non-repeating order.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish general, minimal requirements for face decorations (matching rules) on a 3D monotile to force strong aperiodicity, building upon previous work with the Decorated Chair tile.
main_result: The authors propose simpler matching rules using only face colors, which are shown to be sufficient to force the same strongly aperiodic tiling structure as more complex arrow-based rules.
method: The methodology involves generalizing matching rules through exhaustive enumeration of tile meeting configurations and using inductive proofs based on the hierarchical composition of the tile into 'Superchairs'.
model_or_system: The model is the 3D Decorated Chair tile, which is used to construct a 3D strongly aperiodic tiling. The tiling is characterized as 'limit periodic' and is proposed to be realizable in physical systems like lock-and-key colloids or optical lattices.
key_observables: The number of ways tiles can meet (e.g., reduced from 2388 to 611 with face-color rules) and the resulting diffraction pattern (expected to show purely sharp Bragg peaks).
important_parameters: The dimensionality (3D) and the nature of the decoration rules (arrow colors vs. face colors).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the hierarchical structure (Superchairs) must be obeyed recursively to maintain aperiodicity, and that the proposed face-coloring rules are minimal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Decorated Chair, the Superchair structure, and examples of meeting configurations using both arrow decorations and simpler face-color rules.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the initial proof framework to generalizing the matching rules, testing simpler constraints (arrows, then colors), confirming the hierarchical structure via induction, and finally discussing physical realizations and the minimality of the rules.
why_interesting: While focused on crystallography/tiling theory, the concept of forcing complex, non-periodic order using local rules is analogous to designing quantum error-correcting codes or engineering complex quantum states in optical lattices.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
